0.judgment: Receptivity makes room for progress. Proceed with the steady resolve of a mare, accept guidance when direction is unclear, and find companions where support is available.
0.specialUse: When all six lines change, the special passage favors constancy that can endure.

1.judgment: Return to the path after an interruption. Coming and going can be free of harm; allow time for a cycle of renewal, then move with purpose.

2.judgment: A collective effort calls for discipline and an experienced leader who can keep it orderly.

3.judgment: Conditions favor an approach made with steady purpose. The text warns that a favorable period can turn as the cycle advances.

4.judgment: Modesty supports progress. Stay with your obligations through to the end.

5.judgment: When clarity is obscured, hold to what is right through hardship.

6.judgment: Growth can continue upward. Seek capable guidance and advance without needless anxiety.

7.judgment: The lesser recedes and the greater approaches. Conditions favor open exchange and progress.

8.judgment: Shared enthusiasm can support appointing leaders and organizing a collective effort.

9.judgment: A shock may bring fear before composure returns. Preserve what matters even when the disturbance reaches far.

10.judgment: When tension lifts and there is nowhere to go, return to ordinary conditions. If action remains necessary, take it promptly.

11.judgment: An ill-timed union or commitment can carry disadvantages. The text cautions against pressing ahead.

12.judgment: Small matters are manageable; grand undertakings are out of scale. The passing bird is an image of staying low and close to the ground.

13.judgment: Abundance calls for showing up fully. The text uses the sun at noon as its image of visibility and fullness.

14.judgment: A lasting course brings progress when supported by steadiness and a clear direction.

15.judgment: Great strength is useful when guided by restraint and integrity.

16.judgment: Joining together can be favorable. Examine whether the bond can last; those who come late may lose their place.

17.judgment: Beginnings are difficult even when the potential is good. Build support and give the work structure before setting out.

18.judgment: Danger recurs. Sincerity and inner steadiness allow a person to keep moving through it.

19.judgment: Limits make progress possible, but painful restrictions cannot be sustained indefinitely.

20.judgment: Obstruction calls for a more accessible direction. Seek experienced help and stay steady.

21.judgment: After completion, small matters still need care. An orderly beginning can give way to disorder if attention fades.

22.judgment: A well remains useful even if a settlement moves. The benefit is lost if the water is never drawn or the vessel breaks.

23.judgment: Wait with confidence and persistence. A substantial undertaking remains possible when the time is right.

24.judgment: Gathering people around a shared purpose benefits from capable leadership and a sincere commitment.

25.judgment: Following a sound course can bring progress without blame when guided by steadiness.

26.judgment: Under pressure, staying upright matters more than being believed. The text distinguishes sincere action from words that carry little weight.

27.judgment: Joy and exchange support progress when accompanied by steadiness.

28.judgment: Mutual influence can lead to a favorable union when approached with constancy.

29.judgment: A change earns trust in its proper time. A timely, principled renewal can put regret behind you.

30.judgment: The ridgepole bends under a heavy load. Conditions favor purposeful action to address the strain.

31.judgment: Make the issue known clearly and acknowledge the danger. Start with your own community and avoid escalating to force.

32.judgment: Conditions are breaking down. Advancing further is unlikely to help at this stage.

33.judgment: Examine what you nourish and how you provide for yourself. Keep the means of nourishment sound.

34.judgment: A beginner benefits by actively seeking instruction. Answer a sincere first inquiry and allow time for the lesson to take hold.

35.judgment: A reduction made sincerely can be sound. Even a modest offering can express real commitment.

36.judgment: Stillness comes from setting distractions aside, even when walking among others. The image is composure without blame.

37.judgment: Grace can support limited undertakings. Attend to presentation while keeping the scope modest.

38.judgment: Repair what has deteriorated. Allow time to prepare for the change and to follow through afterward.

39.judgment: Great reserves call for steadiness. Taking nourishment beyond the household and crossing a great river are images of putting accumulated strength to work.

40.judgment: Progress brings recognition. The text pictures a capable lord receiving many gifts and repeated audiences.

41.judgment: Resolving an obstruction may require a clear ruling and the fair application of rules.

42.judgment: The crossing is close to completion, but a young fox wets its tail. Take care with the final steps.

43.judgment: When perspectives diverge, small practical matters can still go well.

44.judgment: Travel offers modest progress. A traveler benefits from steadiness and attention to unfamiliar conditions.

45.judgment: Clarity needs something to sustain it. The image of keeping a gentle cow emphasizes patient care.

46.judgment: The cauldron is a vessel for transformation and nourishment. The judgment speaks of a favorable beginning and progress.

47.judgment: Great possession presents broad opportunities for progress.

48.judgment: The ritual pauses after washing and before the offering. Sincerity and attentive presence matter in the moment of observation.

49.judgment: Increase favors moving forward, including taking on a substantial undertaking.

50.judgment: Dispersion can loosen what has become stuck. A shared purpose, steadiness and a clear crossing can help.

51.judgment: Inner trust reaches even the humble creatures pictured in the text. Sincerity and steadiness support a substantial undertaking.

52.judgment: Development proceeds by stages. The text uses a marriage in due order as an image of steady progress.

53.judgment: A household depends on steadiness in its relationships and responsibilities. The source expresses this through its historical expectations of women.

54.judgment: Gentle, persistent influence can bring modest progress. A clear aim and capable guidance help.

55.judgment: Dense clouds gather without rain. Small restraints can build the conditions for change before results are visible.

56.judgment: Exchange has stalled. Conditions are unfavorable to principled effort as the greater recedes and the lesser takes its place.

57.judgment: Act with sincerity and a sound basis. If the direction is misguided, pressing ahead can bring trouble.

58.judgment: Even a sincere claim can meet resistance. Seek an impartial authority and avoid carrying the dispute to its bitter end.

59.judgment: Treading on a tiger’s tail without being bitten depicts moving carefully through danger and keeping your conduct in order.

60.judgment: A timely withdrawal preserves room to act. Steadiness may still help in smaller matters.

61.judgment: Fellowship beyond familiar circles supports progress and larger undertakings when guided by shared principles.

62.judgment: The text depicts a powerful encounter and cautions against turning it immediately into a lasting commitment.

63.judgment: The Creative points to a strong beginning, growth and benefit sustained by firm purpose.
63.specialUse: When all six lines change, the special passage pictures a group of dragons without a single leader.
